overall: Atlanta is starting the morning at 77.0°F with temperatures completely flat since midnight — not a single degree of movement across all overnight ASOS readings. Broken clouds at a very low ceiling (~488m, ~1,600 ft) with 62% cloud fraction and a high dewpoint of 71.6°F point to a moist, overcast overnight that is likely suppressing the typical pre-dawn radiative cooling and will also limit daytime solar heating. The atmosphere is loaded with moisture, which cuts both ways: a floor is already set high at 77°F, but daytime convective heating will be fought by cloud cover.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show meaningful spread — NBM comes in at 81.9°F, ECMWF at 83.7°F, and HRRR is the aggressive outlier at 86.9°F, a ~5°F gap over NBM. The low ceiling and persistent overnight BKN coverage favor the more conservative NBM solution; HRRR likely expects more cloud erosion than observed conditions currently support. The D1_NOW distribution is notably spread and diffuse (top bucket only 3.7%), reflecting genuine model uncertainty, while the META model concentrates mass in the 86–89°F range — somewhat at odds with the Tier 1 odd-bucket ensemble signal pointing firmly to 81–82°F.
max_temp_prediction: The strongest single ensemble signal is the odd-bucket Tier 1 call of 81–82°F (25.5% probability, 20.4% gap — high confidence tier), and NBM at 81.9°F corroborates the lower end. However, the current temp of 77°F already sets a high floor, and ECMWF at 83.7°F reflects meaningful upside if clouds partially break by early afternoon near the predicted 14h peak. Balancing the suppressive low-ceiling cloud regime and high humidity against the NWP central tendency, the most defensible estimate lands around 83°F — above the odd-bucket center but well below HRRR, with moderate confidence given the cloud uncertainty.
